Nationally, Trump stands at 34 percent approval and 60 percent disapproval, giving him a net approval rating of minus 26.

And this isn't just one poll. Reuters/Ipsos has Trump at 33% as well, with 64% disapproving. More importantly, Reuters reported on August 31 that this was the third consecutive Reuters/Ipsos poll in which his approval remained at 33%.

The economic numbers underneath it are especially rough: the FT/Focaldata poll found 57% saying they're financially worse off under Trump, while nearly two-thirds said the economy is heading in the wrong direction. Nationally, 35 percent of voters approve of Trump's job performance while 59 percent disapprove as of August 19, leaving him significantly underwater with a net approval rating of -24, according to Civiqs' rolling online tracking poll of registered voters. The survey has garnered 124,759 responses since January 20, 2025, when Trump was inaugurated for a second term. [...] In Indiana, Trump's net approval rating slipped underwater in Civiqs' polling in late June, after being positive throughout his second term. It now stands at -3.
